prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Phoenix. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Phoenix for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you targeted names, phone numbers, and short recommendations — but I don’t have live internet access to look up current offices and hours. If you tell me your Phoenix ZIP code or neighborhood (downtown, North/Scottsdale, Ahwatukee, West Phoenix, etc.), I’ll fetch a short list of nearby practices you should call. 

Meanwhile, here are which specific kinds of dental practices to call in Phoenix and why each is useful — plus the exact questions to ask when you call so you can compare them quickly.

Which practices to call (and why)
- Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeons (OMS)
  - Why: OMS specialists handle complex extractions, bone grafting, sinus lifts and implant placement under sedation/general anesthesia. Good for medically complicated cases or full-arch work.
- Periodontists (gum specialists who place implants)
  - Why: Experts in bone and soft-tissue management around implants — ideal if you need grafts or aesthetic gum work.
- Prosthodontists
  - Why: Specialists in the restoration (crowns/bridges/implant-supported dentures). Call them if you want the best-looking, longest-lasting prosthetic teeth, or complex full-mouth rehab.
- Implant-focused multi-specialty centers
  - Why: These coordinate OMS, perio, and prosthodontics in-house — smoother workflow, single treatment plan, and often digital guided surgery.
- University dental clinics (Arizona schools)
  - Why: Lower-cost options with supervised care by experienced faculty — good if price is a major concern and you’re comfortable with trainees.
- Experienced general dentists with extensive implant training
  - Why: Many general dentists place implants routinely with excellent outcomes and lower fees; ask about their training (continuing education, mentorships).

Search resources / directories to find specific names near you
- American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID) “Find an Implant Dentist”
- American College of Prosthodontists “Find a Prosthodontist”
- American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (AAOMS) directory
- ADA Find-a-Dentist, Google Maps, Healthgrades, Yelp (for patient reviews)
- Local dental society referrals (Arizona Dental Association)

What to ask on the phone (use these exact questions)
1. Do you place dental implants in-office, or do you coordinate with a specialist? (If you need both, ask who does the crown work.)
2. How many implants do you place per year, and how long have you been placing them?
3. Do you use CBCT (3D) imaging and guided implant planning? Is that included in the quote?
4. Which implant brands do you use? (Prefer Straumann, Nobel/BioHorizons, Zimmer, etc. — reputable brands)
5. Will bone grafting or sinus lift be needed, and will that be done here?
6. Who will make and deliver the final crown/bridge/denture — the same office or a lab? Do you have an in-house dental lab/technician?
7. What sedation options do you offer? Are IV sedation and anesthesia available if needed?
8. What is the total estimated cost from start to finish, and what’s included (restorations, imaging, grafts, temporaries, follow-ups)?
9. Do you provide a written treatment plan, timeline, and warranty/guarantee on the implant/restoration?
10. Can you show before/after photos of similar cases and provide patient references or reviews?

Other practical tips
- Prioritize practices that offer a single written estimate and a clear timeline.
- Look for recent patient photos of full cases (not just stock images).
- Ask about financing and whether they work with CareCredit or in-house plans.
- If you have medical conditions (diabetes, osteoporosis, smoking, bisphosphonate use), mention that when asking — it affects planning.

If you want specific names, addresses, and phone numbers near you, tell me:
- Your Phoenix neighborhood or ZIP code, and
- Any preferences (specialist type, insurance, budget, sedation needs).

I’ll then provide a shortlist of nearby oral surgeons, periodontists, prosthodontists and implant centers you should call, with a brief reason for each.
